hero.text: Kai was delighted when the kids he rescued cheered his name.

everyday: Grandma was delighted when we surprised her with flowers on her birthday.

contrast.nonExample: Ian felt just okay about getting a plain pencil as a prize.
contrast.explanation: Delighted means very happy. Feeling just okay is not strong enough to be delighted.

items.prompt: Is Jada delighted?
items.passage: When Jada saw the new puppy, she jumped up and down and squealed with joy.
items.hint: How happy does Jada seem?
items.explanation: Delighted means very happy. Jumping and squealing with joy show Jada is delighted.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The kids were ___ when the teacher said there would be an extra recess.
items.clue: an extra recess
items.hint: How do kids feel about extra recess?
items.explanation: Extra recess is great news, so the kids felt very happy. That is delighted.

items.prompt: Which word best describes how Rafi felt?
items.passage: Rafi's team won the big game in the very last second. He jumped, cheered, and hugged everyone.
items.clue: jumped, cheered, and hugged everyone
items.hint: Was Rafi a little happy or very happy?
items.explanation: Jumping, cheering, and hugging show Rafi was very happy, so delighted fits. Fine is only a little happy, which is too weak.

wrong.c: Fine means just okay. Rafi's cheering and hugging show much stronger happiness.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what delighted means.

chunks.text: so she hugged her aunt and grinned.
so she frowned and said nothing.

items.hint: Delighted people show they are very happy.
items.explanation: Hugging and grinning show great happiness. Frowning shows Tess was not pleased.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "delighted" in this sentence?
items.passage: The audience was delighted by the funny puppet show.
items.hint: How would people feel at a funny show they love?
items.explanation: Thrilled means very happy and excited, close to delighted. Bored is the opposite.

hero.text: Bolt was annoyed when the alarm kept beeping during his nap, so he turned it off.

everyday: I get annoyed when my sister hums the same song over and over.

contrast.nonExample: Pia screamed and threw her backpack when her brother smashed her model ship.
contrast.explanation: Annoyed means only a little angry. Screaming and throwing things show someone is furious, which is much stronger.

items.prompt: Which person is annoyed?

options.text: Cam sighs and rolls his eyes when a fly keeps buzzing near him.
Cam laughs and laughs at a funny joke his best friend tells him.
Cam shakes with fear during a storm.

items.hint: Who is bothered by something small?
items.explanation: Annoyed means a little angry or bothered. Sighing and rolling his eyes at a buzzing fly shows Cam is annoyed.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Dad was ___ because the dripping faucet kept him awake all night.
items.clue: dripping faucet kept him awake
items.hint: How would a dripping sound all night make you feel?
items.explanation: A dripping faucet that keeps you awake is bothersome, so Dad felt annoyed.

items.prompt: Which word best describes how Mila felt?
items.passage: Mila's friend was ten minutes late. Mila tapped her foot and sighed, then said hello.
items.clue: tapped her foot and sighed, then said hello
items.hint: Is Mila a little bothered or extremely angry?
items.explanation: Tapping her foot and sighing show Mila was a little bothered, but she still said hello. That is annoyed. Furious would mean extremely angry, which is too strong.

wrong.a: Furious means extremely angry. Mila only sighed and still said hello, so she was just annoyed.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what annoyed means.

chunks.text: so he sighed and sharpened it.
so he cheered and danced around.

items.hint: Annoyed people are a little bothered.
items.explanation: Sighing shows Jay was a little bothered. Cheering and dancing show happiness, not annoyance.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Ms. Diaz?
items.passage: The barking dog next door kept bothering Ms. Diaz while she tried to read.
items.clue: kept bothering
items.hint: How does a noise that keeps bothering you make you feel?
items.explanation: "Kept bothering" shows Ms. Diaz felt a little angry about the noise. That is annoyed.

definition: able to wait calmly without getting upset

hero.text: Juniper stayed patient while the scared puppy slowly crept out from under the car.

everyday: Mr. Lin is patient and explains the math problem again when we don't understand.

contrast.nonExample: Eli honked the horn again and again because the line of cars was not moving.
contrast.explanation: Patient people wait calmly. Eli got upset and honked, so he was impatient.

items.prompt: Is Ava being patient?
items.passage: Ava waited quietly in the long lunch line without complaining.
items.hint: Does Ava wait calmly?
items.explanation: Patient means able to wait calmly. Ava waits in a long line without complaining.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: You have to be ___ when you fish, because a bite can take a long time.
items.clue: a bite can take a long time
items.hint: What do you need when something takes a long time?
items.explanation: "Can take a long time" means you must wait calmly. That is being patient.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "patient" in this sentence?
items.passage: The patient boy waited his turn on the slide.
items.hint: Look for a word that means NOT able to wait calmly.
items.explanation: Impatient means not able to wait calmly, the opposite of patient.

items.prompt: The prefix im- means "not." What does "impatient" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The impatient kids in the back seat kept asking, "Are we there yet?"
items.hint: Im- + patient = not ___.
items.explanation: Im- means not, so impatient means not patient: not able to wait calmly. Asking "Are we there yet?" over and over shows it.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Kim?
items.passage: Kim spent weeks building a model ship piece by piece and never rushed.
items.clue: spent weeks; piece by piece; never rushed
items.hint: Kim worked a long time without hurrying.
items.explanation: "Spent weeks" and "never rushed" show Kim calmly kept going for a long time. That is patient.

definition: having good manners and treating others with respect

hero.text: After saving the bus, Rex gave the driver a polite nod and said, "Have a nice day."

everyday: It is polite to say "please" when you ask for something.

contrast.nonExample: Drew grabbed the last slice of pizza and burped loudly at the table.
contrast.explanation: Polite means using good manners. Grabbing food and burping at the table are rude.

items.prompt: Which person is polite?

options.text: Sara holds the door open and says, "After you."
Sara cuts in front of everyone in line.
Sara talks loudly while others are speaking.

items.hint: Who is using good manners?
items.explanation: Polite means having good manners. Holding the door and saying "After you" is polite. Cutting in line and talking over people are rude.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ boy said "excuse me" before he walked past the teacher.
items.clue: said "excuse me"
items.hint: Saying "excuse me" shows what?
items.explanation: Saying "excuse me" is good manners. That is polite.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "polite" in this sentence?
items.passage: The polite waiter smiled and refilled our water glasses.
items.hint: Which word means bad manners?
items.explanation: Rude means having bad manners, the opposite of polite. Kind is close to polite, not opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what polite means.
items.hint: Polite people let others finish.
items.explanation: Waiting until someone finishes talking is good manners. Yelling over a friend is rude.

items.prompt: Which line is polite?

options.text: "Hand me that book right now, because I want it more than you do."
"May I please borrow your book when you're done?"
"That book is boring, just like you."

items.hint: Which speaker uses good manners?
items.explanation: "May I please" and waiting until the person is done show good manners. That is polite. The other lines are bossy or mean.

definition: hard to find because there is very little of it

hero.text: Water was scarce in the desert town, so Nova flew in big tanks to help.

everyday: Fresh strawberries are scarce in winter, so they cost more at the store.

contrast.nonExample: There were so many apples on the tree that the branches bent to the ground.
contrast.explanation: Scarce means there is very little. The tree had plenty of apples, so they were plentiful, not scarce.

items.prompt: Were shells scarce on this beach?
items.passage: The beach had more shells than we could ever pick up.
items.hint: Were there a few shells or a lot?
items.explanation: Scarce means there is very little. This beach had tons of shells, so they were plentiful, not scarce.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Food was ___ in winter, so the squirrels ate the nuts they had saved.
items.clue: ate the nuts they had saved
items.hint: Why would squirrels need to eat saved food?
items.explanation: The squirrels used saved nuts because there was very little food around. That means food was scarce.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "scarce" in this sentence?
items.passage: Pandas are scarce in the wild, so people work hard to protect them.
items.hint: Why would people need to protect them?
items.explanation: Rare means there are very few, like scarce. Pandas need protection because there are so few in the wild.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what scarce means.

chunks.text: used both sides of every sheet.
threw away whole stacks of it.

items.hint: When something is scarce, you try not to waste it.
items.explanation: Using both sides saves paper when there is very little. Throwing away stacks only makes sense if paper is plentiful.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the tickets?
items.passage: Only three tickets were left for the concert, and hundreds of people wanted them.
items.clue: Only three tickets were left; hundreds of people wanted them
items.hint: Are there enough tickets for everyone?
items.explanation: "Only three" tickets for "hundreds of people" means there were very few. That is scarce. Plentiful is the opposite.

definition: showing good sense; wise and practical

hero.text: Kai made a sensible plan: get everyone out of the building first, then catch the robot.

everyday: Wearing warm boots in the snow is a sensible choice.

contrast.nonExample: Ned wore flip-flops to hike up a steep, rocky mountain.
contrast.explanation: Sensible choices are wise and practical. Flip-flops on a rocky trail are an unwise choice.

items.prompt: Which choice is sensible?

options.text: wearing a heavy coat on a hot beach
taking an umbrella on a rainy day

items.hint: Which choice is wise?
items.explanation: Sensible means wise and practical. An umbrella on a rainy day keeps you dry.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: It was ___ of Kate to save part of her allowance for later.
items.clue: save part of her allowance for later
items.hint: Is saving money a wise choice?
items.explanation: Saving money for later is a wise, practical choice. That is sensible.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "sensible" in this sentence?
items.passage: Packing a snack for the long car trip was a sensible idea.
items.hint: Sensible means wise. What is the opposite of wise?
items.explanation: Foolish means unwise, the opposite of sensible.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what sensible means.
items.hint: A sensible person makes the safe, wise choice.
items.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the wise, safe choice, so it is sensible. Riding without one is not.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Mrs. Ortiz?
items.passage: Before the storm, Mrs. Ortiz filled jugs with water and found her flashlight.
items.clue: Before the storm; filled jugs with water; found her flashlight
items.hint: Is getting ready before a storm wise?
items.explanation: Getting water and a flashlight ready "before the storm" is wise and practical. That is sensible.

definition: able to bend easily without breaking

hero.text: Pixel's flexible suit let her bend and twist through the narrow pipes.

everyday: A rubber band is flexible, so you can stretch it and it snaps back.

contrast.nonExample: The dry stick snapped in half when Lucas tried to bend it.
contrast.explanation: Flexible things bend without breaking. The dry stick broke, so it was stiff, not flexible.

items.prompt: Is the ruler flexible?
items.passage: Mia bent her plastic ruler into a curve, and it sprang back without breaking.
items.hint: Did the ruler bend without breaking?
items.explanation: Flexible means able to bend without breaking. The ruler curved and sprang back.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Gymnasts are very ___ and can bend over to touch their toes easily.
items.clue: bend over to touch their toes easily
items.hint: What word means able to bend easily?
items.explanation: "Bend over" and "easily" show the gymnasts' bodies bend well. That is flexible.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "flexible" in this sentence?
items.passage: The flexible straw bent so I could drink while lying down.
items.hint: What do you call something that will NOT bend?
items.explanation: Stiff means hard to bend, the opposite of flexible.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what flexible means.
items.hint: Flexible things bend but don't break.
items.explanation: A flexible branch bends without breaking. Snapping right away shows a stiff branch.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Dad's body now?
items.passage: Doing yoga every morning helps Dad's body stretch and bend more easily than before.
items.clue: stretch and bend more easily
items.hint: What does yoga help Dad do?
items.explanation: "Stretch and bend more easily" means Dad's body is more flexible. Fragile would mean it breaks easily.

hero.text: Bolt recalled the robot's weak spot from their last battle and aimed right for it.

everyday: Can you recall the name of your first-grade teacher?

contrast.nonExample: Jen forgot where she left her shoes and had to search the whole house.
contrast.explanation: To recall is to bring a memory back. Jen could not remember, so she forgot instead of recalling.

items.prompt: What does "recall" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: I can recall every word of my favorite poem.
items.hint: Saying every word of a poem from memory means you...
items.explanation: Recall means to remember. You bring every word back from memory.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Do you ___ where we parked the car this morning?
items.clue: where we parked; this morning
items.hint: The question asks about something that happened earlier.
items.explanation: Parking happened "this morning," so you must remember it. That is recalling.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "recall" in this sentence?
items.passage: Grandpa likes to recall stories from when he was a boy.
items.hint: Recall means remember. What is the opposite?
items.explanation: Forget is the opposite of recall. Grandpa remembers his stories instead of forgetting them.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what recall means.

chunks.text: because she had studied it the night before.
even though she had never learned it.

items.hint: You can only recall something you learned before.
items.explanation: Sara recalled the answer because she studied it earlier. You can't remember something you never learned.

items.prompt: Which word best tells what Jon did?
items.passage: Jon closed his eyes and thought hard until the phone number came back to him.
items.clue: the phone number came back to him
items.hint: The number "came back" into Jon's mind.
items.explanation: "Came back to him" means Jon remembered the number. That is recalling. Predicted is about the future, not memory.

definition: to trust and depend on someone or something

hero.text: The whole city can rely on Nova to show up whenever there is trouble.

everyday: Plants rely on sunlight and water to grow.

contrast.nonExample: Eva's alarm clock often stops working, so she never knows if it will ring.
contrast.explanation: To rely on something, you must be able to trust it. Eva can't trust her alarm, so she can't rely on it.

items.prompt: Does Max rely on his sister?
items.passage: When homework is hard, Max asks his big sister, because she always helps him.
items.hint: Does Max trust and depend on his sister?
items.explanation: To rely on someone is to depend on them. Max counts on his sister because she always helps.

items.prompt: Choose the words that best complete the sentence.
items.passage: Baby birds ___ their parents to bring them food.
items.clue: to bring them food
items.hint: Baby birds can't get food alone. What do they do?
items.explanation: Baby birds can't feed themselves, so they depend on their parents "to bring them food." That is relying on them.

items.prompt: Which words are closest in meaning to "rely on" in this sentence?
items.passage: You can rely on Tia to keep a secret.
items.hint: Can you trust Tia with a secret?
items.explanation: Count on means trust and depend on, the same as rely on. You can trust Tia to keep a secret.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what rely means.

chunks.text: We rely on our bus driver

items.hint: You rely on people you can trust.
items.explanation: Being on time every day makes the driver someone you can trust, so we rely on her. You can't rely on someone who is always late.

items.prompt: Which sentence tells about the farmer and his tractor?
items.passage: The farmer needs his tractor every single day to plow his fields.
items.clue: needs his tractor every single day
items.hint: What does needing something every day tell you?
items.explanation: "Needs his tractor every single day" shows the farmer depends on it. That is relying on it.

definition: worried or a little scared about what might happen

hero.text: Kai felt nervous before his first big rescue, and his hands shook a little.

everyday: Ella was nervous before her piano recital, so she took slow, deep breaths.

contrast.nonExample: Ty smiled and strolled onto the stage, relaxed, for his tenth show.
contrast.explanation: Nervous means worried or jumpy about what might happen. Ty was calm and relaxed, so he was not nervous.

items.prompt: Which person is nervous?

options.text: Ben bites his nails, and his tummy flips before the spelling bee.
Ben naps happily on the couch.
Ben eats a big turkey sandwich with chips at the lunch table.

items.hint: Who is worried about something that is about to happen?
items.explanation: Nervous means worried about what might happen. Biting nails and a flipping tummy before the spelling bee show worry.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Olivia felt ___ while she waited for the doctor to give her a shot.
items.clue: waited for the doctor to give her a shot
items.hint: How do many kids feel waiting for a shot?
items.explanation: Waiting for a shot makes many people worried about what will happen. That is nervous.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "nervous" in this sentence?
items.passage: The nervous cat jumped at every little noise.
items.hint: The cat jumped at every noise.
items.explanation: Jumpy means easily startled and on edge, close to nervous. "Jumped at every little noise" is the clue.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what nervous means.

chunks.text: so he studied extra the night before.
so he didn't think about it at all.

items.hint: Nervous people worry about what is coming.
items.explanation: Worrying about the test made Lucas study extra, which fits nervous. Not thinking about it at all shows no worry.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Zoe?
items.passage: Before her first swim race, Zoe's heart pounded and she kept worrying she would come in last.
items.clue: heart pounded; kept worrying
items.hint: Is Zoe happy, angry, or worried?
items.explanation: A pounding heart and "kept worrying" before the race show Zoe was nervous. A pounding heart can come with anger too, but she is worried, not angry.
